unit.why: A short anecdote: the widowed Maggid of Kozhnitz refuses to remarry, and the Seer of Lublin sends word that his prayers are not ascending, so he remarries. It is framed by a Zohar-based ruling.

stories.start_quote: בסה"ק זוהר חי על הזוהר ויקרא
stories.end_quote: ותיכף קיים דבריו ונשא עכ״ל עיי״ש
stories.summary_en: Citing the Zohar rule that a man without a wife may not lead public prayer, the text tells how the Seer of Lublin sent word to the Maggid of Kozhnitz, widowed past seventy and unwilling to remarry, that his prayers did not ascend properly, and the Maggid at once remarried.

tags.why: Remarriage is the outcome and the subject

quotes: כל תפלות שלו לא עלו כהוגן
tags.why: The issue is whether his prayers are valid and ascend

quotes: דמי שאין לו אשה אסור להתפלל להוציא הרבים
tags.why: A prohibition on an unmarried man leading public prayer

quotes: אסור להתפלל להוציא הרבים כי עבודתו פסולה
tags.why: The story turns on a legal-mystical rule about who may lead prayer

quotes: כל תפלות שלו לא עלו כהוגן לא נהירין ולא בהירין
tags.why: The Seer knows from afar the heavenly state of another man's prayers

quotes: ולא רצה עוד לישא אשה כי כבר נתבטל ממנו הכח
tags.why: He chooses to stay celibate after his wife's death
